name: llama.cpp under ROCm on 2x RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100): Qwen3.8-27B Q4_K_XL batch-1 tensor-split decode throughput
methodology: PER-REQUEST decode throughput, batch 1, single stream - explicitly framed as the llama-server serving case for one user at a time on this hardware class. Tensor-split across 2x RX 7900 XTX under ROCm on gfx1100. Model Qwen3.8-27B at Q4_K_XL, 17.545 GB, which streams once per token at batch 1. Accompanying measured arithmetic, which is the reason this is worth a record: the pair moves 825.7 GB/s = 43.0% of their combined 1920 GB/s DRAM peak, leaving 57% of aggregate bandwidth idle. Single-card baseline is 632.5 of 960 GB/s = 65.9% UMC on the faster card, 623.5 on the other. So adding a second card delivers only 1.31x throughput despite neither card being bandwidth-saturated. The issue decomposes this into a 1.518x solo-inefficiency factor and a 1.532x tensor-split penalty, 2.326x combined. OMITTED BY SOURCE: exact llama.cpp commit and ROCm version, prompt length, generation length, KV-cache size, thread count, which ROCm backend path, and clock state. Projections in the issue (72.1 tok/s at per-card-equal efficiency, 109.4 tok/s at 100% UMC) are explicitly labelled projections from measured bandwidths and are NOT recorded as measurements.
notes:
Valuable precisely because it quantifies a failure mode that generic tok/s figures hide: consumer-RDNA multi-card tensor parallelism underperforms badly on consumer cards, where the only link between GPUs is PCIe rather than a fabric. 1.31x for 2x the hardware is a poor result, and the per-card DRAM utilisation drops from 65.9% to 43.0% when the split is introduced - the split actively makes each card less efficient. Cross-checked against a second model in the same issue: a 7B at Q8_0 keeps 63.9% of its solo per-card bandwidth when split, so the penalty is a roughly constant fraction that multiplies whatever the batch-1 kernel already achieves. PRACTICAL TAKEAWAY: on RDNA, do the arithmetic before assuming a second card buys you a second card's worth of tokens per second. ACCELERATOR ID CAVEAT: no accelerators/amd-radeon-rx-7900-xtx record exists in this repo; planned id, validator will warn. measured_by third_party and status draft: community research issue, no build or version pinned. The underlying measurement (47.06 t/s, 825.7 GB/s, 65.9%/43.0%) is concrete and cross-checked within the issue; the derived percentages are the author's own arithmetic on those measurements.

So a value here does NOT mean the interconnect was exercised by this particular workload, and must not be cited as evidence that it was. Whether the run actually crossed that fabric is a question about TP/EP/PP size, which this repo records in methodology, not here. NOT INVENTED: nothing was filled where the accelerator record itself carries no interconnect, so this field stays empty for any part whose own record has none - which is the honest state for a single-socket Apple sOC and for parts whose vendor publishes no host interface.
